A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PRISM and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The complete 19-page v1 and 25-page v2 support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original backdoor-defense experiments, baseline comparisons, component ablations, adaptive attacks, and a medical-domain trust-chain case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds experiments on auditor collusion, target classes, victim architectures, poisoned initialization, semantic-consistent triggers, and image captioning.

M1.justification: The classification algorithm and existing trust-chain procedure are retained. Appendix S adds a limited captioning adaptation: image-caption CLIP similarity replaces the per-class logit margin, and per-class statistics and prototype refinement are dropped while statistical gating remains.

E1.justification: v2 adds Flickr30k image captioning, extending evaluation beyond classification. It also tests target-class semantic blending, partially coordinated auditor backdoors, and entirely poisoned initialization batches. These extend task and input-environment coverage; the earlier classification datasets and medical case study remain.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets remain. New Table 17 evaluates nine training-time defenses: ABL, DBD, ASD, D-BR, EP, ReBack, PIPD, MSPC, and CGD. Table 18 adds Fine-Pruning, ANP, and an unpoisoned-model control. The training-time comparison explicitly involves different data-access assumptions.

E3.justification: New protocols include five GTSRB targets evaluated under nine attacks, additional MobileNetV2/VGG-16/ViT victims, clean versus fully poisoned initialization at three stream poison rates, and blending ratios from 0.1 to 0.5 with a clean-model control. Captioning introduces CIDEr and target-caption ASR. Existing benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.5.3 and Appendices N–R add substantial analyses of auditor-backdoor coordination, target-frequency sensitivity, victim-architecture robustness, dirty cold-start behavior, and semantic-trigger strength. These investigate additional failure conditions beyond v1's retained component ablations, mixed-stream attacks, feature mixing, and trust-chain study.

E5.justification: Appendix S adds explicit distributional spread reporting for caption-audit scores: 0.306±0.044 for clean inputs and 0.010±0.056 for backdoored inputs, with a stated 6.7σ separation. This is not repeated-run uncertainty. Neither version specifies seeds or repeated-run counts, and Appendix N's significance claim lacks a specified test.

E6.justification: Matched existing numerical tables are unchanged, including Table 1's 93.2% average CA and 0.8% ASR. Substantial new results include 100% ASR under full auditor collusion versus at most 0.8% in the other tested scenarios, dirty cold-start ASR up to 10.9%, and captioning ASR falling from 100% to 0% while CIDEr changes from 62.6 to 61.2. These are newly reported experiments, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Appendices R–S introduce mathematical definitions for target-feature blending and the caption-level audit statistic. The Cornish-Fisher derivation, online moment equations, and prototype-update mathematics are retained; no new theorem or proof is provided.

C1.justification: The central claims remain external semantic auditing, online adaptation through the Hybrid VLM Teacher and Adaptive Router, and strong performance across 17 datasets and 11 attacks. The stronger data-free emphasis restates a constraint already present in v1 rather than establishing a new core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of partial versus full auditor collusion, text-anchor protection during poisoned initialization, and the boundary between backdoors and genuinely target-like blended images. Section 6 and Appendix U expand limitations and proposed mitigations, including sequence-task adaptation and few-shot assistance. Conversely, v1's explicit bias, hallucination, and fairness caveat is omitted.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the anonymous code pointer with a named GitHub repository and explicitly specifies first-subword log probabilities for generative classification scores. New appendices document experimental configurations, exclusions, and captioning backbones. The main implementation settings, warm-up rules, hyperparameters, and prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands cited literature and positioning, adding connections to reward auditing, prototype evolution, memory systems, federated robustness, and broader application domains. It also situates PRISM against training-time defenses and introduces references for pruning comparators and captioning. These additions exceed the accompanying bibliographic updates to retained works.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and impact statement are rewritten to emphasize data-free deployment. v2 adds a Discussion section, combines the two trust-chain appendix sections, and fixes the unresolved distribution-validation reference. Most existing methodological and experimental prose remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven distinct tables covering collusion, target classes, victim architectures, cold-start conditions, training-time defenses, semantic blending, and captioning. Existing figures retain their graphics, although Figures 3 and 4 exchange numbering and placement. Several retained tables are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 improves scrutiny of robustness through controlled poisoned-initialization tests, additional victim architectures and targets, and semantic-consistent attacks with a clean-model control, which v1 did not provide. The gain is limited by underqualified new interpretations: Appendix N supplies no test for its significance claim, and Table 18 does not show uniformly lowest ASR despite the superiority wording. The core results and theoretical support remain unchanged.
